historical_growth.basis: Pre-merger Omnicom standalone series (FY2019-FY2024); the combined entity has no history. These describe the business that was, and are used only as a reasonableness check on the forward paths.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (pre-merger standalone, FY2021-FY2024, 3.2%), cross-checked to FY2026 organic guidance of ~5% and the holding-company industry's 2-3% long-run organic rate; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 7.9% exceeds revenue 3.2% and EPS 4.7% by >30%: book value grew because buybacks fell to ~$370-600M/yr against ~$1.5B of earnings, not because the business compounded faster. FY2025 equity ($12.7B) then tripled on IPG share issuance. Equity CAGR is not a growth signal here.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2019 $1,621.0M, FY2021 $1,167.6M, FY2024 $1,400.6M. The 5-year owner-FCF CAGR (-2.9%) is below the reported FCF CAGR (-1.9%) because interest income rose from $60M to $101M on a larger cash pile; SBC was stable at ~0.6% of revenue. FY2022 ($848M reported) was a working-capital trough, not an operating one.

scenario_narratives.base: The integration lands roughly as guided: six creative networks become three without major client losses, the $750M-$1.5B synergy programme reaches the ~$1B run-rate during FY2027, and Core Operations grow 3% then 2.5% a year as a 'Big 3' scale media buyer with a data platform. EBITDA margin settles at 18.5% (EBITA ~17.7%) once the last ~$200-300M of cash severance and integration costs roll off in FY2027-28. FCF is deployed to the $5B buyback and the $3.20 dividend, which the model treats as value-neutral. The axes are organic growth versus the 2-3% industry rate, synergy capture net of dis-synergies, and whether the market's 7x adjusted P/E persists -- the 12x FCF exit cap assumes a modest re-rating toward Omnicom's own history, not toward the market.
scenario_narratives.bull: Scale and data become a real moat: media-buying leverage against Google, Meta, Amazon and retail media networks plus Omni/Acxiom/Kinesso identity data lift organic growth to 4-5.5% through FY2029 with $3B+/yr of new-business billings, synergies reach the $1.5B top of the range and margins expand to 19.8% EBITDA (EBITA ~19%, Publicis-level). The buyback retires ~20% of the count at single-digit multiples and the stock re-rates toward a 14x FCF exit. Needs three things to go right at once -- growth, margin and multiple -- which is why the weight is 20%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The merger scales up the problem rather than solving it: AI-native creative and self-serve media tools and advertiser in-housing erode the intermediary role, client conflicts across the combined roster force resignations, and talent leaves with the retired DDB/FCB/MullenLowe brands. Revenue declines 1-2% a year from FY2028, synergies are given back in pricing, EBITDA margin drifts to 15%, and the exit multiple is 9x FCF. Leverage (2.4x) stays serviceable but the $5B buyback is in hindsight capital spent on a melting asset. The 30% weight reflects that this is the branch the current price is already discounting and that integration execution is unproven for at least four more quarters.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the combined Omnicom-IPG entity on a normalised FY2026 Core Operations run-rate, not on FY2025 GAAP (one month of IPG, $1.25B of repositioning charges, negative net income) or on the pre-merger standalone history. Unlevered owner FCF is built from an adjusted-EBITA-plus-depreciation margin with SBC expensed and the share count held flat, acquired-intangible amortisation ignored as non-cash and non-deductible, operating leases left inside operating cost, and three debt-like claims deducted in the bridge: net debt, non-controlling interests and the unpaid cash severance. Cash integration costs are charged in the FY2027-28 margins rather than adjusted away. The three scenarios carry the integration and structural-decline risk in their flows and weights; WACC is the same 8% in all three so that risk is charged once. Terminal value is capped at 9-14x FCF, below the sector's pre-2022 multiples, because the market's 7x P/E is itself evidence that a Gordon-growth exit is not something a buyer has to grant.
key_risks_to_valuation: Integration execution: client defections or talent attrition during the six-to-three network consolidation would show up first as organic growth below the 5% FY2026 guidance and would move the base case toward the bear path
Structural AI disintermediation: if self-serve platforms and in-housing compress agency revenue faster than the bear case's -1 to -2% a year, the 15% bear margin and 9x cap are not the floor
Synergy give-back: the FY2027-28 margin step-up assumes 75-80% of the $900M 2026 synergy flows to EBITA; competitive pricing or reinvestment could hold margins at the ~16.5% pre-merger combined level
Terminal multiple: the 12x base cap sits above today's ~9.5x EV/owner-FCF; if the market never re-rates, intrinsic value is overstated by roughly the gap between the two multiples on the FY2036 FCF
Leverage and rates: 2.4x gross leverage with ~$10B of notes; a cyclical ad downturn would cut FCF while the $5B buyback and $0.80 quarterly dividend are being funded
Disposal proceeds and remaining restructuring cash are both estimates: proceeds are carried at zero (upside) and the $341M severance liability at book (could rise if further actions are announced)
FTC consent order and five-year compliance monitor add a compliance cost and client-relationship friction not separately modelled

inputs.base_revenue_basis: FY2026E Core Operations revenue (net of dispositions and held-for-sale businesses), combined Omnicom+IPG. Anchored to H1 2026 Core Operations revenue of $11,610.7M (10-Q, +6.9% vs combined H1 2025, 5.0% organic) grossed up on a 48% H1 seasonal share. FY2025 reported revenue of $17,271.9M carries only ~5 weeks of IPG and is NOT the base; FY2024 and earlier describe the pre-merger standalone company.
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 274,345,967 shares on the Q2 2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-22) plus ~1.1M dilutive awards (Q2 2026 weighted diluted 281.0M less basic 279.9M). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the $5.0B post-merger buyback ($2,988.2M spent in H1 2026 incl. the $2.5B ASR, ~$1.5B authorization remaining to April 2027) is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral in this model.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30 June 2026 10-Q: notes payable $9,953.2M + short-term borrowings $48.8M = $10,002.0M total debt; cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash $3,336.2M. Net debt $6,665.8M ties to the MD&A's stated $6.7B. Finance leases (~$105M) and operating lease liabilities (~$1.9B) are excluded from debt -- see lease_treatment.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: FY2026E estimate, levered, GAAP: adjusted net income ~$2.93B (guided high-teens growth on the $8.65 2025 base, ~287M average diluted shares) less after-tax amortization, integration and repositioning costs (~$600M), plus D&A ~$670M and SBC ~$115M, less capex ~$265M, working capital assumed neutral = reported FCF ~$2,850M. Owner FCF = 2,850 - 125 (SBC incl. withholding) - 150 (interest income) = 2,575. NOTE: the engine projects UNLEVERED owner FCF from EBITDA, so its FY2027 figure sits ~$250-300M above last_fcf by the after-tax net interest expense that last_fcf still carries; the debt cost is charged through WACC and the net-debt bridge, not the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: Q2 2026 10-Q cash flow statement share-based compensation $52.9M for H1 2026 (annualised ~$115M); FY2025 10-K $100.8M (Omnicom standalone + 5 weeks IPG), FY2024 $91.4M. Withholding on net-share settlement ~141k shares in Q2 2026 (~$10M/yr) added to reach $125M. No company-published combined figure.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026E ~$150M (H1 2026 $76.9M). Stripped from last_fcf because the $3.3B cash that earns it is netted against debt in the bridge; leaving both would count the cash twice. The EBITDA-based projection is pre-interest, so nothing further is needed in the paths.
inputs.buyback_cash_note: H1 2026 actual financing outflow (10-Q), including the $2.5B accelerated share repurchase. FY2025 was $707.9M, FY2024 $370.7M. Management guides ~$3.5B for calendar 2026 and completion of the $5.0B authorization by April 2027.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-01T20:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 66.33-89.57
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~9.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (2026 notes issued at 4.2-5.3%) x (1-26%) = 3.7%; capital structure ~65% equity ($20.6B market cap) / 35% debt ($10.0B) -> 7.6%, rounded up to 8.0% for a cyclical, people-based business carrying 2.4x gross leverage. The same 8.0% is used in all three scenarios: structural-decline and integration risk are charged ONCE, in the bear scenario's flows and its 30% weight, not again through the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Omnicom is a US GAAP filer whose operating-lease cost ($239.3M FY2025; occupancy and other costs ~$1.0B H1 2026 incl. IPG footprint) sits inside operating expenses and therefore inside the EBITDA margin path. Operating lease liabilities ($1.41B non-current at 30-Jun-2026 plus current) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is depreciation only (0.85% of revenue, H1 2026 $98.1M), excluding both right-of-use amortisation (already in the lease cost) and acquired-intangible amortisation (non-cash and, for the stock-for-stock IPG deal, largely non-deductible: ~$470M/yr post-merger is neither deducted from EBITDA nor added back).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, in the bridge: non-controlling interests $610.4M (equity) + redeemable NCI at fair value $318.8M at 30-Jun-2026 = $929.2M deducted from enterprise value. Flows are left unattributed (NCI's profit share ~$70-100M/yr, FY2025 $98.2M, H1 2026 $34.2M; capitalised at ~9-10% it is ~$750-1,000M, so the book+fair-value deduction is the conservative end).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) via make build-dcf -- Omnicom is an operating services company whose value is a stream of free cash flow; routing row 1 of dcf-methods/SKILL.md; adaptations file applied for leases, NCI and charging risk once. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry). MERGER NORMALISATION: the IPG all-stock acquisition closed 2025-11-26, so FY2024 and earlier are a different (standalone) entity and FY2025 is a transition year (-$54.5M net income on $1,247M of Q4 repositioning charges; shares 196M -> 313M; debt $6.1B -> $9.3B). fy0 is therefore FY2026E on the company's own Core Operations basis (net of dispositions and held-for-sale businesses that carried $1.2B of H1 2026 revenue at a ~7% EBITA margin); the explicit horizon runs FY2027-FY2036. EBITDA margin = adjusted EBITA margin (Core, H1 2026 16.4%, Q2 17.8%) plus depreciation ~0.8pp; the FY2027 and FY2028 base-case margins are haircut ~0.8pp and ~0.3pp for residual cash integration and repositioning costs ($184.9M pre-tax in H1 2026), so the paths are after those costs, not 'adjusted'. The $341.0M of unpaid cash severance and contract-termination liabilities at 30-Jun-2026 is a debt-like claim deducted in the equity bridge. Held-for-sale businesses have NEGATIVE net assets at net realisable value (assets $808.1M vs liabilities ~$1,052M), so disposal proceeds are carried at zero; any net cash received is upside not in the model. Working capital is modelled as neutral (wc_capture 0): media payables exceed receivables so growth has historically been cash-neutral-to-positive over a cycle, but FY2022-FY2024 saw $170-500M/yr of outflows and no capture is credited. Cash tax 26% = the company's own non-GAAP adjusted effective rate (Q2 2026 26.0%), applied to unlevered EBIT; the Pillar Two minimum is below that. Buybacks beyond the SBC offset are value-neutral under the flat-count convention even though at 7x adjusted P/E they would be accretive; that upside is deliberately not modelled. The CSV FY2025 EBITDA (721.4) and net income (-54.5) are post-charge GAAP figures and are not used as a base.

bear.rationale: The structural-decline branch the 7x adjusted P/E is pricing: AI-native self-serve platforms and client in-housing shrink the agency intermediary role, merger client conflicts and talent attrition bite, revenue declines 1-2%/yr from FY2028, synergies are consumed by pricing pressure so EBITDA margin drifts back to 15% (below the pre-merger combined level), 9x exit cap.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 3.0% then fading to 2.5%: management's ~5% FY2026 organic guidance rides a soft IPG 2025 comparison and $3.3B of H1 new-business billings; the long-run holding-company organic rate is 2-3% and merger client conflicts typically cost 1-2pp. No FX credited.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026E Core adjusted EBITA ~16.8% + depreciation 0.8% = 17.6% EBITDA. FY2027 underlying ~18.4% (synergies at the $1B+ run-rate) less ~0.8pp residual cash integration/repositioning cost = 17.6%; FY2028 underlying 18.8% less 0.3pp = 18.5%; mature 18.5% EBITDA = ~17.7% EBITA, between Omnicom's standalone 15.5-16% and Publicis' ~19-20%.
base.terminal_rationale: 12x FCF cap binds (Gordon at 8%/2% would be 17x). 12x is below Omnicom's own 2015-2021 EV/owner-FCF range (~12-14x) and above today's ~9.5x; a lower cap is used because the business is cyclical and structurally slower-growing.

bull.rationale: Synergies reach the $1.5B top of the range and the scale/data platform (Omni + Acxiom/Kinesso) wins share: organic growth holds 4-5.5% through FY2029, EBITDA margin 19.8% (EBITA ~19%, Publicis-level), 14x exit cap (still below the sector's pre-2022 multiples).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 30% from the 15% house default: the thesis rests on an unproven two-holdco integration (6 networks to 3, 4,000+ job cuts, three retired brands) and the sector faces a live structural question from AI disintermediation that the 7x adjusted P/E says the market takes seriously. Bull cut to 20% because it needs growth, margin and a re-rating to all land. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
